summary: Image checkpoints are keyed by the full image identity, not a 30-bit seed
compatibility: No user action required. Image checkpoints saved by earlier builds are not reused and recompute once; text checkpoints are unaffected.
details: Two different images could get the same boundary-checkpoint key (about 1 in a billion per pair, and constructible on purpose), so one image's cached state could be restored for another.
Every image position now carries independent bits of the image's content hash, and no checkpoint ends within an image's first five tokens.
